_comment: Per-finding gosec waivers for code outside Phase 0/Part 0 (W1-W6)/Phase 1 scope, per the Phase 0 CI harness item's pre-existing-findings policy (.SPECIFICATION/IMPLEMENTATION.md). Every entry names one exact (file, line, rule) finding gosec currently reports and a reason; it is not a blanket rule or directory exclusion. A finding that stops matching (because the surrounding code moved) must be re-reviewed, not silently re-added: that is deliberate, not a maintenance burden to route around. Every entry's backstop is AGENTS.md's own rule: gosec must be validated (zero remaining waivers) prior to Phase 20 production packaging.

Owned by Phase 11 (API Gateway & Telemetry). Phase 11 audited this exact finding and closed the underlying risk rather than only re-waiving it: jobID is now rejected unless it parses as a UUID (internal/api/logs.go's StreamLogs), so the value gosec still traces from the chi URL param into this SSE write can no longer contain a newline, an angle bracket, or any other character with meaning to an SSE consumer or a browser. The same check closed a real NATS subject-wildcard injection on the line below it (FAILURE_PATTERNS.md). gosec's taint analysis cannot see the uuid.Parse guard, so the finding remains reported; it is no longer reachable. Re-verify at Phase 39.

Owned by Phase 14 (The Dispatcher) / Phase 39, not this phase's own checklist. json.Encode error ignored writing the dispatch-accepted response, the same low-risk after-headers-sent pattern already waived in hateoas.go above. Line numbers shifted again (154-159 -> 171-176) when Phase 12 removed the per-device auth.CheckAccess call and its comment above this line (FAILURE_PATTERNS.md #66: the check was redundant with api.RequireScope, which now enforces the same scope once at the router boundary); no code at this finding itself changed.
